newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-FIFA TO KEEP KEY WORLD CUP GAMES ON FREE TV.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-FIFA TO KEEP KEY WORLD CUP GAMES ON FREE TV.

text.p: FIFA general secretary Sepp Blatter said on Wednesday that key World Cup matches such as the the final would remain on "free" television.
"The opening game, one semifinal and the final... They will be shown on free television," Blatter told the SoccerEx 97 conference, referring to the World Cups in 2002 and 2006.
FIFA last year signed a $2.2 billion World Cup television rights deal with Bavarian media mogul Leo Kirch and Swiss-based marketing agency ISL covering those two tournaments.
The two companies will sell the rights but FIFA retains a veto over who buys them.
Blatter did not rule out pay television companies securing rights to some games, noting that not all broadcasters want every game in a 64-match tournament.
Two weeks ago UEFA, European soccer's governing body, said it backed the idea of major matches and tournaments staying on public access TV and not sold off to the highest bidder.
Blatter had lunch with British Prime Minister John Major but refused to be drawn on the row between England and Germany over their rival bids to host the 2006 World Cup.
"The fact we already have a fight for 2006 means the FIFA World Cup and soccer is a good product," he said.

Players' agents at the conference urged FIFA to crack down on clubs who flout regulations by using unlicensed middlemen to conduct transfer deals. A group of some 70 FIFA-approved agents have formed their own association and are now threatening to publish a blacklist of unlicensed brokers.

"We are genuinely trying to clean up this act," said Jon Smith, a leading British agent. He cited the example of Norwegian Rune Hauge who continues to act for players despite being banned from working as an agent by FIFA.
"There are regulations and FIFA has teeth. Now it needs to bite," Smith added.
The licensed agents want clubs who break the rules to be banned from European competition or have their right to buy players suspended.
